title: Uniform-in-time square-root Hele–Shaw convergence for singular-pressure flows with uniformly convex confining and compatible interaction potentials
source_title: Improved convergence rates for the Hele-Shaw limit in the presence of confining potentials
author: Noemi David; Alpár R. Mészáros; Filippo Santambrogio
difficulty_reason: Contractivity and the general transport derivative do not bound the singular nonlinear diffusion defect when densities can vanish and there is no common positive lower bound. The authors combine the Monge–Ampere density ratio with the pressure complementarity and the sign of the singular Laplacian to obtain a uniform O(epsilon) defect, then symmetrize the interaction drift and isolate the barycenter term for both convexity alternatives. This quantitative free-boundary/transport comparison is the nonroutine remaining obligation beyond the precise prior existence, optimal-transport and Grönwall foundations.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Selected singular pressure p_epsilon=epsilon*rho/(1-rho), global branch of Theorem2.4. Nonnegative potentials V,W on R^d with bounded Hessians, W even, D²V>=alpha I with alpha>0, D²W>=beta I and alpha+beta>0. Common initial probability density has finite second moment, zero barycenter and sup norm<=1. Wasserstein-two distance to the unique incompressible weak flow is O(sqrt(epsilon)) uniformly for all nonnegative time. Full singular-pressure proof16–21 read, including drift/interactions18–19, Monge–Ampere complementarity diffusion20 and contractivity21. Named AGS gradient-flow/transport differentiation12–13 and prior Hele–Shaw weak solution theory3–4 are background. Porous-medium dyadic-exponent branch and stationary variants are not selected. PDF13/2026/322 and author spelling verified.

historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: The authors combine the Monge–Ampere density relation with one-sided pressure complementarity to bound the nonlinear diffusion defect, symmetrize the nonlocal drift and exploit transport contractivity to obtain a uniform-in-time quantitative incompressible limit. This nonlinear free-boundary transport analysis exceeds ordinary qualifying examinations.
